cases.sentence: ___ Николай Андреич Болконский в декабре 1805 года получил письмо от князя Василия, извещавшего его о своем приезде вместе с сыном.
cases.explain: «Старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Old Prince Nikoláy Andréevich Bolkónski received a letter from Prince Vasíli in November, 1805, announcing that he and his son would be paying him a visit. “I am starting on a journey of inspection, and of course I shall think nothing of an extra seventy miles to come and see you at the same time, my honored benefactor,” wrote Prince Vasíli. “My son Anatole is accompanying me on his way to the army, so I hope you will allow him personally to express the deep respect that, emulating his father, he feels for you.”

cases.sentence: — Вот Мари и вывозить не нужно: женихи сами к нам едут, — неосторожно сказала ___, услыхав про это.
cases.explain: «маленькая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It seems that there will be no need to bring Márya out, suitors are coming to us of their own accord,” incautiously remarked the little princess on hearing the news.

cases.sentence: Через две недели после получения письма, вечером, приехали вперед люди князя Василья, а на ___ приехал и он сам с сыном.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: A fortnight after the letter Prince Vasíli’s servants came one evening in advance of him, and he and his son arrived next day.

cases.sentence: Старик Болконский всегда был ___ о характере князя Василья, и тем более в последнее время, когда князь Василий в новые царствования при Павле и Александре далеко пошел в чинах и почестях.
cases.explain: «невысокого мнения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Old Bolkónski had always had a poor opinion of Prince Vasíli’s character, but more so recently, since in the new reigns of Paul and Alexander Prince Vasíli had risen to high position and honors. And now, from the hints contained in his letter and given by the little princess, he saw which way the wind was blowing, and his low opinion changed into a feeling of contemptuous ill will. He snorted whenever he mentioned him. On the day of Prince Vasíli’s arrival, Prince Bolkónski was particularly discontented and out of temper. Whether he was in a bad temper because Prince Vasíli was coming, or whether his being in a bad temper made him specially annoyed at Prince Vasíli’s visit, he was in a bad temper, and in the morning Tíkhon had already advised the architect not to go to the prince with his report.

cases.sentence: Теперь же, по намекам письма и ___, он понял, в чем дело, и невысокое мнение о князе Василье перешло в душе князя Николая Андреича в чувство недоброжелательного презрения.
cases.explain: «маленькой княгини» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Old Bolkónski had always had a poor opinion of Prince Vasíli’s character, but more so recently, since in the new reigns of Paul and Alexander Prince Vasíli had risen to high position and honors. And now, from the hints contained in his letter and given by the little princess, he saw which way the wind was blowing, and his low opinion changed into a feeling of contemptuous ill will. He snorted whenever he mentioned him. On the day of Prince Vasíli’s arrival, Prince Bolkónski was particularly discontented and out of temper. Whether he was in a bad temper because Prince Vasíli was coming, or whether his being in a bad temper made him specially annoyed at Prince Vasíli’s visit, he was in a bad temper, and in the morning Tíkhon had already advised the architect not to go to the prince with his report.

cases.sentence: Однако, как обыкновенно, в 9-м часу князь вышел гулять в своей ___ с собольим воротником и такой же шапке.
cases.explain: «бархатной шубке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: However, at nine o’clock the prince, in his velvet coat with a sable collar and cap, went out for his usual walk. It had snowed the day before and the path to the hothouse, along which the prince was in the habit of walking, had been swept: the marks of the broom were still visible in the snow and a shovel had been left sticking in one of the soft snowbanks that bordered both sides of the path. The prince went through the conservatories, the serfs’ quarters, and the outbuildings, frowning and silent.

cases.sentence: ___ не была нездорова; но она до такой степени непреодолимо боялась князя, что, услыхав о том, как он не в духе, она решилась не выходить.
cases.explain: «Маленькая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: His plate seemed to him not quite clean, and pointing to a spot he flung it away. Tíkhon caught it and handed it to a footman. The little princess was not unwell, but had such an overpowering fear of the prince that, hearing he was in a bad humor, she had decided not to appear.

cases.sentence: Вообще маленькая княгиня жила в Лысых Горах постоянно под чувством страха и антипатии к ___, которой она не сознавала, потому что страх так преобладал, что она не могла ее чувствовать.
cases.explain: «старому князю» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: In general at Bald Hills the little princess lived in constant fear, and with a sense of antipathy to the old prince which she did not realize because the fear was so much the stronger feeling. The prince reciprocated this antipathy, but it was overpowered by his contempt for her. When the little princess had grown accustomed to life at Bald Hills, she took a special fancy to Mademoiselle Bourienne, spent whole days with her, asked her to sleep in her room, and often talked with her about the old prince and criticized him.

cases.sentence: Маленькая княгиня сидела за ___ и болтала с Машей, горничной.
cases.explain: «маленьким столиком» — after the preposition «за», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: After dinner, he went to see his daughter-in-law. The little princess was sitting at a small table, chattering with Másha, her maid. She grew pale on seeing her father-in-law.

cases.sentence: Анатоль сидел, сняв камзол и подпершись руками в бока, перед столом, на угол которого он, улыбаясь, пристально и рассеянно устремил свои прекрасные ___.
cases.explain: «большие глаза» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Anatole, having taken off his overcoat, sat with arms akimbo before a table on a corner of which he smilingly and absentmindedly fixed his large and handsome eyes. He regarded his whole life as a continual round of amusement which someone for some reason had to provide for him. And he looked on this visit to a churlish old man and a rich and ugly heiress in the same way. All this might, he thought, turn out very well and amusingly. “And why not marry her if she really has so much money? That never does any harm,” thought Anatole.

cases.sentence: Так же и теперь он смотрел на свою поездку к злому старику и к богатой ___.
cases.explain: «уродливой наследнице» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Anatole, having taken off his overcoat, sat with arms akimbo before a table on a corner of which he smilingly and absentmindedly fixed his large and handsome eyes. He regarded his whole life as a continual round of amusement which someone for some reason had to provide for him. And he looked on this visit to a churlish old man and a rich and ugly heiress in the same way. All this might, he thought, turn out very well and amusingly. “And why not marry her if she really has so much money? That never does any harm,” thought Anatole.
